newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks mixed in directionless market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks mixed in directionless market.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares were mixed in a directionless market on Thursday but brokers said they were beginning to see prices bottoming up after being depressed by profit-takers over the past two weeks.
"The market is showing no direction but we are starting to see the bottom and some buyers creeping back," one broker said.
"But I don't see much happening on the market until after the Christmas and New Year holidays," he added.

The 57-share industrial index nudged up a marginal 0.96 points to close Thursday at 8,054.77 after local conglomerate TA Holdings and textiler David Whitehead gained 10 cents each to 160 and 90 respectively.

House appliances-maker Capri, discount house DCZ, packaging firm Hunyani and battery-maker Chloride -- which registered higher share earnings for the year ended September 30 despite stiff competition from cheaper imports -- all added five cents to 130, 185, 355 and 100 respectively.
Among the losers, Alloys fell 100 cents to 750 while finance group Finhold at 860 and sugar producer Hippo at 900 both shed 10 cents.
Minings were largely lacklustre with gold producer Rio Tinto sliding 100 cents to 3,200 and copper counter Mhangura five cents down at 20.
The seven-stock mining index lost 10.16 points to 1,168.06.
